broad_context: Short basic exercises in edublocks Scratch editor for learning algorithmic thinking.
exercise_prompt: Ask the user for their name and print out a message that says "Hello, {name}".
exercise_context: The user must use the scratch blocks sensing.ask; looks.say; variable.set; operators.join.

broad_context: Short basic exercises in edublocks Scratch editor for learning algorithmic thinking.
exercise_prompt: Ask the user for two numbers, and then print out the sum of the two numbers.

broad_context: Short basic exercises in edublocks Scratch editor for learning algorithmic thinking.
exercise_prompt: Ask the user for their age, and then print out a message that says "You were born in: {year}".

broad_context: Short basic exercises in edublocks Scratch editor for learning algorithmic thinking.
exercise_prompt: Ask the user for a temperature in Celsius, and then print out the temperature in Fahrenheit.  The formula for converting from Celsius to Fahrenheit is F = C * 9/5 + 32.

broad_context: Short basic exercises in edublocks Scratch editor for learning algorithmic thinking.
exercise_prompt: Ask the user for the number of days, and then print out how many weeks and days that is.

broad_context: Short basic exercises in edublocks Scratch editor for learning algorithmic thinking.
exercise_prompt: Ask the user for a password, and then print out "Access granted" if the password is "Open Sesame".

broad_context: Short basic exercises in edublocks Scratch editor for learning algorithmic thinking.
exercise_prompt: Ask the user for a number, and then print out "Even" if the number is even, and "Odd" if the number is odd.

broad_context: Short basic exercises in edublocks Scratch editor for learning algorithmic thinking.
exercise_prompt: Ask the user for the current hour, and then print out "Good morning" if the hour is before 12, "Good afternoon" if the hour is between 12 and 18, and "Good evening" if the hour is after 18.
exercise_context: Use the blocks operators.<; operators.>; operators.and (optional).

broad_context: Short basic exercises in edublocks Scratch editor for learning algorithmic thinking.
exercise_prompt: Ask the user for the current hour (in 24-hour format), and then print out the current hour in 12-hour format, followed by "AM" or "PM". You can assume that the minutes are always 0. Bonus: make sure that this still works if the hour is higher than 23! E.g. 24 -> 0:00 AM, 25 -> 1:00 AM
exercise_context: Combine previously learned blocks. Use control.if_else; operators.=; operators.+; operators.- . Use operators.mod for hours greater than 23.

broad_context: Short basic exercises in edublocks Scratch editor for learning algorithmic thinking.
exercise_prompt: Ask the user for a number, and then print out "Hey" that many times.

broad_context: Short basic exercises in edublocks Scratch editor for learning algorithmic thinking.
exercise_prompt: Ask the user for a number, and then count down from that number to 0, printing out each number.
exercise_context: Use the blocks operator control.repeat or control.repeat_until.

broad_context: Short basic exercises in edublocks Scratch editor for learning algorithmic thinking.
exercise_prompt: Ask the user for a number, and then keep doubling that number until it is greater than 1000, and print out the result. Also print out how many times you had to double the number.

broad_context: Short basic exercises in edublocks Scratch editor for learning algorithmic thinking.
exercise_prompt: Print out the numbers from 1 to 100, but replace every number that is divisible by 3 with "Fizz", every number that is divisible by 5 with "Buzz", and every number that is divisible by both 3 and 5 with "FizzBuzz".
exercise_context: Use previously learned blocks. Use operators.mod and operators.= for checking divisibility. Use control.if_else for determining what to print.

broad_context: Short basic exercises in edublocks Scratch editor for learning algorithmic thinking.
exercise_prompt: Ask the user for an interest rate (in percent), a number of years, and an initial amount of money. Print out how much money the user will have after the given number of years, assuming that the interest is compounded annually. Hint: for each year, you will need to multiply the amount of money by (1 + interest rate / 100).
exercise_context: Use previously learned blocks. Use control.repeat or control.repeat_until for the number of years. Use operators.+; operators./; operators.* for calculating the new amount of money each year.

broad_context: Short basic exercises in edublocks Scratch editor for learning algorithmic thinking.
exercise_prompt: Ask the user for the number of sides of a polygon, and then draw that polygon (i.e. 3 -> a triangle, 4 -> a square, 5 -> a pentagon). To draw, you will need to use the pen extension, which you can activate by clicking on the extension button in the bottom left corner of the screen, and then clicking on the pen extension.
exercise_context: Use the blocks pen.pen_down; motion.move; motion.turn_right . Use operators./ to calculate the angle to turn at each corner (360 / number of sides).
